code.text: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the left breast mass and the left axillary node: invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 3; estrogen receptor 95 percent, progesterone receptor 85 percent, HER2 1+ (negative), Ki-67 30 percent; the node contains metastatic carcinoma

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Urgent surgical oncology (breast) consultation for a biopsy-proven, node-positive breast cancer, to plan the operation and the axilla
  • Same-week diagnostic mammography and ultrasound of both breasts and both axillae, and ultrasound-guided core biopsy of the mass and the abnormal node with ER, PR, and HER2 testing
  • Genetic counseling and germline multigene panel testing (including BRCA2, BRCA1, PALB2, CHEK2, and ATM), as for every man with breast cancer, with a letter for relatives if a variant is found
  • Mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection, then shoulder exercises and lymphedema risk reduction with arm measurements at each visit
  • Adjuvant chemotherapy given by medical oncology (doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide every three weeks for four cycles, then weekly paclitaxel for twelve weeks, about six months), after a baseline echocardiogram, hepatitis B screening, vaccines, and a dental review; radiation oncology review of post-mastectomy radiation after chemotherapy
  • Tamoxifen after chemotherapy for at least five years, the first-choice endocrine therapy for men, with venous thromboembolism, mood, hot flash, sexual side effect, and adherence checks at every visit
  • Distress screening at each visit, plain information that men get breast cancer, confidential handling of his diagnosis at work, and the offer of a peer-support group for men with breast cancer

resource.title: Richard Roundtree synthetic care plan
resource.description: Men get breast cancer. Evaluate a new breast lump in a man of 51 promptly, without accepting an earlier history of gynecomastia as an explanation: examination that tells a firm, eccentric cancer from soft, central gynecomastia, same-week diagnostic mammography and ultrasound of both breasts and both axillae, and core biopsy of the mass and any abnormal node; ER, PR, and HER2 status; germline genetic testing and counseling for every man with breast cancer; surgical planning with a breast surgical oncologist; lymphedema prevention; and preparation for chemotherapy followed by tamoxifen, the preferred endocrine therapy for men, on the ASCO male breast cancer guideline, the NCCN breast guideline, and the CMID breast cancer monograph. His own public account of embarrassment and of keeping his treatment secret frames the teaching on the stigma that delays men's care.
